title: Investing in Augmented Reality – Trevor Doerksen – Medium
text: Apr 1 Investing in Augmented Reality In 2017, there was nowhere in Los Angeles or Silicon Valley a person could go and not hear about Virtual Reality (VR) — many ignored the warnings about the VR hype. A new Canadian public company, the only public company in North America, focused instead on Augmented Reality (AR). AR enhances a users existing environment, where VR replaces it. AR minimally requires only a newer Apple or Android phone and a rear-facing camera. ePlay’s AR Advertising Platform launched prior to AR being available on iPhone in August 2017. Still in 2017, ePlay and its recently added subsidiary, Mobovivo took to adding Augmented Reality to Mobovivo’s proprietory game engine. ePlay leads as one of the only software stock plays in North America. The company uses the Mobovivo Game Engine to deploy games for ESPN, FIFA World Cup, Los Angeles Lakers, Time Warner Cable, Sportsnet, Hannibal TV series, Sony Pictures, Cineplex and others. ePlay started working on AR months before Apple’s new AR Kit was available on iPhone and Google’s ARCore was available on Android. ePlay invested in AR research and development in order for Mobovivo, ePlay’s business-to-business subsidiary to offer the technology to brands, teams and leagues starting in 2017. ePlay’s AR Ad Kit platform was available a month prior to Apple releasing AR on its phones in August 2017. When Apple released iOS11 with ARKit a month later, Apple CEO, Tim Cook said, “Simply put, we believe augmented reality is going to change the way we use technology forever,” “Augmented reality is going to change everything,” Cook said. In March 2018, Apple released an update to its ARKit technology that helps the rear-facing camera of an iPhone or iPad detect the users surroundings even better. “The sports AR game we call PokeSports internally, keeps improving as Apple and Google update their ARKit and ARCore software development kits,” says Trevor Doerksen, CEO of ePlay Digital. “Anybody we show the games we are developing to loves what they see.” ePlay is due to release its first AR game for NBA very soon and given the March ARKit update from Apple, this helps set the stage for release. Eplay has taken that idea a step further to reinvent fantasy sports and provide traditional leagues concerned over waning audiences a toolset to engage younger audiences — something the company refers to as “Poké-sports. The name of the new game title is soon to be released and has NBA legend Rob Horry and sports reporter Lindsay McCormick as part of the ePlay and can be recruited by end users in AR to join users’ teams. If you agree with Apple’s CEO and with ePlay, how can investors get involved in AR? Investors of Apple AAPL and Facebook FB know that both are involved in AR hardware and software. Facebook is developing an AR headset and accompanying software. Other mixed hardware /software investment stock opportunies include: Google GOOGL , Nintendo NTDOY , Alibaba BABA , Intel INTC , Imagination Park ( IPNFF ) , Microsoft MSFT , Vuzix VUZI ,and Amazon AMZN . T he only publicly-trade Augmented Reality software companies in the market include: Shopify , ePlay Digital ( EPY ), and Snap . Why should you care? The AR Market grew from $6B in 2016 to $11B in 2017 with estimates of $143B by 2020. ePlay is in development on 4 Augmented Reality titles to be released in 2018. At the same time, Warner is looking to release an AR title for Jurassic Park and Niantic a Harry Potter AR title in 2018. Statista Augmented Reality Projections
